shots.desc: Split screen: left an ordinary kid practises piano while a calendar flips DAY 1→10; right Eli practises while a clock advances only 1 hour. Both reach the SAME result together (gold notes) and a big "=" appears.
Close-up on Eli at the piano, playing fluently and smiling; the clock behind him shows only one hour passed.
Top-down piano keys lighting up in a fluent melody (match-cut source). "1 HOUR = 10 HOURS".
Match cut: piano keys become a laptop keyboard; fast typing.
Keyboard becomes a textbook page under a desk lamp; "1 DAY = 10 DAYS".
The page folds into a football tactics board; an arrow draws the play; pull-out reveals it.
School exterior at dusk; Eli and Noah walk to school; title card WHAT IF YOU COULD LEARN ANYTHING 10x FASTER? glows in.
Heroic low angle: Eli in the hallway, blinding backlight, rim light on both edges, lens flare; camera spins in like a superhero reveal.
Flat awkward classroom wide: teacher at the ENGLISH board points at Eli: "Eli. The answer?"
Eli medium shot, hand half-raised, confidently wrong: "Uh... thirty-seven?"
Extreme close-up on the teacher's unamused eyes behind her glasses: "We're in English class." The ENGLISH board is visible behind.
Class laughs (extras rocking with laughter); Eli sinks in his chair.
Close-up Eli, deflated, chin on desk.
Football field: Eli winds up (anticipation), swings, whiffs just over the ball, lands flat on his back with a thud; the ball dribbles away toward the goal.
Side-profile piano: Eli hits awful notes, winces on each one; keys flash red.
Overhead under a lamp: a sheet of music flutters down and becomes a math test with a huge red F.
Outside school at dusk: Eli slumped on a bench; Noah (yellow cap, blue shirt) walks in holding his own D- test and drops onto the bench.
Over Eli's shoulder (Eli seen from behind, foreground): Noah, deadpan, looking at Eli: "Dude, we're so cooked."
Reverse over Noah's shoulder: Eli, flat: "You think?"
Dawn establishing: the view from Eli's window at sunrise; 6:00 AM.
At his desk at dawn, Eli rubs his eyes over messy notes; DAY 7 on the wall calendar (a week of struggle).
Notebook insert under lamplight: messy crossed-out working, a red question mark.
Extreme close-up pencil under lamplight: the messy steps rearrange themselves into a clean ordered solution (the pattern clicks).
Close-up: Eli's eyes widen — a double-take in the dawn light.
Overhead page: problem after problem gets a green tick, tick, tick.
Proof graphic over a dimmed desk: timer 00:00→06:00; BEFORE bar = 60 MIN, NOW bar stops at 6 MIN (one tenth); "SAME UNDERSTANDING".
Beat of silence, then Eli close-up facing camera with the BEWILDERED look (callback face for the ending): "Wait... what?"
Overhead: Eli's old F math test; his hand (sleeve entering from frame edge) re-does it; red crosses flip to green ticks one by one, then a big green 6/7 stamp lands over the F.
Extreme close-up: Eli stares at the result, a slow grin spreading.
The rule card: "LEARNS 10× FASTER FROM PRACTICE" with crossed-out myths: instant knowledge, superhuman body, perfect judgment. Eli thinking beside it.
Dawn bedroom: Eli springs up from the desk with an eager grin and cracks his knuckles.
Music room wide at sunset: upright piano waiting; label EXPERIMENT 1 · PIANO.
Eli at the piano, cocky: "Okay. How hard can this be?"
Overhead hands: wrong keys flash red, discordant notes, camera jolts on each clunker.
Eli wincing close-up as the narrator deadpans "Pretty hard, apparently."
Time-lapse: sunlight slides across the room, the clock spins one hour, Eli practises with less and less fumbling; PRACTICE bar fills to 60 MIN.
Music moment (no VO): slow lateral dolly along the keyboard as Eli plays the full melody; correct keys glow gold and release floating note shapes.
Field at sunset: Eli tries to trap the ball; it bounces off his shin and rolls away. He facepalms.
Extreme low angle beside the ball: Eli taps it up again and again; dotted trajectory lines get tighter and tidier each rep; REP counter climbs.
Wide: a clean skill move — Eli flicks the ball up and volleys it into the goal; the net bulges; he celebrates.
Noah arrives at the touchline, jaw on the floor: "Bro, since WHEN could you do that?!"
Eli, juggling, shrugs, equally amazed: "I don't know!"
Flashcard HOLA flips to こんにちは, flips again; the practice timeline at the bottom keeps filling.
The flashcard slides into a laptop screen: code types, an ERROR appears, gets fixed, BUILD OK.
The coded animation (a little bouncing gold ball) hops out of the screen into the real bedroom.
Eli close-up, delighted, eyes following the bouncing ball.
Limits #1: Eli asleep with his head on his open textbook at 2:00 AM, lamp still on — he still needs sleep.
Limits #2: on the field Eli dribbles neatly, but a bigger kid simply out-sprints him to the ball. Labels SKILL ✓ / SPEED · STRENGTH ✗.
SAME classroom angle as S008 (deliberate repeat). MATH on the board now; teacher asks; Eli raises his hand confidently.
Match cut: the old F test is swept aside by a new test stamped A+.
Teacher close-up: her glasses slide down her face in genuine surprise.
Students crowd around Eli's desk holding out notebooks and questions.
Hallway: friends point at things on the lockers — a guitar, a chess-club flyer, a basketball poster; Eli grins eagerly at each one.
Classroom: Eli seated at his desk (left, looking up); a cocky student in a green cap stands behind the desk and slaps a scrambled Rubik's cube down: "Bet you can't solve this."
Eli close-up, sly confident smile: "Give me ten minutes."
Obsession montage A: Eli centred, front-on; a puzzle cube then a chessboard swap in front of him; friends behind him lose patience and walk away; light shifts warm → cool.
Obsession montage B: same framing; a book then a circuit diagram; the background is now empty; cool blue light.
Alone in the cold light: Eli's phone lights up on the desk — "Noah: hey, wanna hang out?" — and without looking up from his circuit diagram he flips it face-down with his own hand.
Robotics workshop, warm afternoon: Eli and Noah build the robot together and high-five. Two benches: Eli's (left, with a photo of the two friends) and Noah's (right, blue tool tray).
Robot close-up: red stripe (Eli) and blue stripe (Noah) side by side — built together; both their hands (sleeves entering from the frame edges) tighten parts.
A poster on the workshop wall: ROBOTICS CUP — WINNER QUALIFIES FOR STATE FINALS; a calendar beside it flips through months.
Calendar on the workshop wall: months flip by — they spent months building it.
Pace contrast: Eli types at blurring speed (motion-trail arms, code scrolling) while Noah slowly turns pages of a manual.
Noah, eager, holds up his sensor drawing and points at it: "the metal barriers could confuse this sensor. I added a backup on the left..." Eli works at his bench, half-listening.
Insert of Noah's diagram: METAL barrier note, BACKUP sensor labelled LEFT; then the real robot's blue backup box on its left side lights up (labelled).
Reverse angle from Noah's side (shelves behind): Eli, seated at his bench with his back three-quarter to Noah, doesn't look up: "Already fixed it." Noah's sentence is cut off.
Over Eli's shoulder (Eli from behind, foreground): Noah tries again, "Oh. Well, what about the steering?"
Top-down over Eli's bench: his hands type on the laptop; Noah's hand slides his diagram in — Eli pushes it aside without looking: "Fixed that too."
Noah close-up, hurt: "Dude, can I at least do something?" The music has dropped out.
Over Noah's shoulder: Eli, back turned, still typing: "I mean... I'll probably finish it faster."
HOLD on Noah in silence (no music). He hesitates, then slowly lowers his small blue screwdriver onto his bench in the foreground — one isolated click — head dropping.
From the workshop doorway: Noah walks out toward camera and past it without a word; behind him Eli, small, keeps working at his bench, back turned. Noah's screwdriver lies on his empty bench.

One fixed wide over several afternoons: sunlight sweeps across the workshop again and again; Eli alone works faster, the robot gets more polished; Noah's bench stays empty (his screwdriver still lying there); the photo of the two friends sits on Eli's bench.
Close-up: Eli glances at the empty stool, then back to work. Cool light.
Tournament hall wide: ROBOTICS CUP banner, floodlights and haze, crowd in the bleachers, course table with metal barriers.
Eli alone at the team station; the name card reads TEAM: ELI & NOAH (Noah is still officially registered). Telephoto: Noah, arms crossed, in the crowd under a pale beam.
Telephoto: Noah, arms crossed, sitting in the crowd under a pale beam — he came, but not as part of the team.
Low tracking shot beside the robot racing along the table: table seams and blurred foreground posts whip past, speed lines behind it.
Whip to overhead: the robot zips through the course corners at speed, motion-blurred.
Overhead course: the robot weaves around the barriers along the dotted route and finishes — ROUND 1 ✓, then ROUND 2 ✓.
Announcer with headset mic, arm thrown out to the side (face clear): "And Eli's team advances to the final!" Crowd cheers.
Scoreboard flips to FINAL, clock starts at 0:60 in red; the music tightens.
Robot POV rushing toward a shiny METAL barrier; the orange main-sensor LED flickers.
Overhead: the robot suddenly veers the wrong way and bumps the barrier; red wrong-route line; clock running.
Eli panics, hands on his head: "No, no, no. WHAT?!"
Diagnostic laptop: SOFTWARE ✓ OK, MOTORS ✓ OK — nothing wrong found; the timer keeps falling.
Eli frozen at the station, the crowd blurred and muffled; the timer ticks.
Cutaway: the robot stuck against the barrier, wheels spinning, orange LED flickering.
Extreme close-up on Eli's eyes: this isn't something he can learn his way out of.
Eli looks up; a telephoto shot isolates Noah (yellow cap) in the crowd, picked out by a pale beam.
Eli shouts across the hall: "NOAH!"
Geography wide from behind Eli at the station: across the hall, Noah stands up in the bleachers: "What?!"
High angle over Noah's shoulder down to Eli at the station: "Remember that sensor setup...? Why did you want to change it?"
Noah close-up, frustrated: "Because the metal barriers mess with the readings! I told you that three weeks ago!"
Cutaway under Noah's line: the robot still jammed against the metal barrier, wheels spinning, orange LED flickering.
Sepia flashback that exactly matches S059: Noah holding up the diagram and pointing (BACKUP · LEFT, METAL); Eli not listening; the soft tool-click returns.
Back in the hall: Eli freezes — guilty realisation.
Low angle on Eli, the timer large in the foreground: "Okay! What do I do?!"
Telephoto push on Noah in the bleachers, pointing hard to his left: "Switch to the backup sensor! LEFT SIDE!"
Tight on the controller: Eli's thumb flips the switch MAIN → BACKUP SENSOR; zap.
Extreme close-up on the real robot's rear-left corner (wheel + chassis + the blue BACKUP box from S060): its LED ignites and spills blue light across the chassis.
Close overhead on the metal barrier: lit by its blue backup LED, the robot curves cleanly AROUND the barrier this time (blue trail) instead of veering into it.
Overlay explaining why it worked: the main sensor's reading near metal is jagged; the backup sensor's reading is clean.
Overhead: the robot races the rest of the route toward the finish; clock 0:03 → 0:02.
Extreme close-up of the red timer hitting 0:01. The music cuts out.
Slow-motion close-up: the robot creeps toward the checkered line in silence but for a heartbeat; its front wheel touches the first checker exactly on the horn — flash, crowd, and the triumph theme.
The crowd erupts under golden light, confetti falls; scoreboard WINNER 0:01.
An official's hand lifts the trophy in the foreground; Eli glances at it, then his eyeline moves past it, screen-right, toward Noah (rack focus trophy → Eli).
Eli walks away from the trophy, threading through the cheering crowd toward Noah — sheepish, determined.
Two-shot by the bleachers, applause softening, golden light: Eli, sincere: "Dude... I'm sorry." Noah, arms crossed: "For what?"
Over Noah's shoulder: Eli: "Thinking I didn't need you."
Noah's soft, unreadable reaction — then the corner of a smile.
Over Eli's shoulder: Noah, teasing: "Yeah, that was pretty stupid."
Low profile wide, blurred applauding crowd in the foreground: Eli laughs "You're telling me." — Noah bumps his shoulder; Eli rocks sideways and they both laugh.
Dusk outside the school: the two friends walk home together through the warm door-light, carrying the robot and the trophy; camera pans with them.
The robot's red and blue stripes side by side in warm light; the camera drifts to the friends' photo propped next to it.
Match cut to the opening piano (overhead keys): Noah's hand hits a terrible note.
Music room: Noah at the piano: "So... you gonna teach me that piano song or what?" Eli walks in and sits down beside him.
Overhead keys (same angle as S002/S105): Eli's red-sleeved hands play the first two bars of the song, clean and gold, next to Noah's blue sleeve — "Yeah."
Noah, seated at the piano (keyboard edge in frame), cheerfully: "Cool. It'll only take me ten hours."
Callback: Eli, seated, turns to camera with exactly the same bewildered face and framing as "Wait... what?" (S026): "...Oh my God." Silent beat, comedic sting, hard cut to black.
Title on black: WHAT IF YOU COULD LEARN ANYTHING 10x FASTER?
